paragraphs: AutoGO improves neural networks by editing their computation graphs: the collections of basic operations that carry out a model’s calculations. This connects model design with deployment efficiency. Instead of searching only among predefined architectures, the framework can change both individual operations and larger pieces of a network through the same graph representation.

The approach converts graph components into tokens and mutates segments of varying sizes. Its supporting techniques identify frequently occurring segments and use a pretrained predictor to estimate how replacing a segment will affect the network in context. Together, these components provide a way to explore changes at multiple scales while considering their likely consequences.

Experiments show improvements in task performance alongside reductions in floating-point operations across classification, segmentation, human pose estimation, and super resolution, without adding new primitive operations. Tests of optimized super-resolution and denoising U-Nets on an NPU cycle simulator also show improved PSNR with lower latency and power. These results support graph-level evolution as a route toward models that combine useful predictions with more efficient execution.
neurips-2023-autogo-automated-computatio.tldr: AutoGO evolves neural networks by replacing computation-graph segments, improving task performance and deployment efficiency in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: The paper studies collaborative data analysis where users communicate with a server while facing both privacy concerns and communication limits. Compressing messages reduces the amount sent, but it also discards information. The central question is whether mechanisms producing a small, discrete set of possible outputs can provide quantifiable privacy protection as well as communication savings.

Using f-differential privacy, the authors derive tight, closed-form local privacy guarantees for several discrete mechanisms. These include binomial methods designed for privacy and sign-based methods designed for compression. This puts mechanisms with different original purposes into a common privacy framework and makes their protection mathematically explicit.

The authors also examine how sparsification can amplify privacy and introduce a stochastic compressor with three possible output values. For distributed mean estimation, their approach uses compression’s privacy benefits to remove the dependence of mean squared error on communication cost that appears in existing methods. The claimed break in the three-way tradeoff concerns this estimation setting, showing how compression can contribute to privacy rather than serving solely as a source of information loss.
neurips-2023-breaking-the-communication-.tldr: The paper quantifies privacy from discrete compression and uses it to decouple mean-estimation accuracy from communication cost.

paragraphs: Many causal discovery methods infer graph structure by testing whether two variables become independent after accounting for other variables. With limited data, these tests become less reliable when they account for many variables at once. This paper studies what can be learned when the number of conditioning variables is deliberately capped at an integer k.

That restriction changes which graphs the available tests can distinguish. The authors define k-Markov equivalence: two graphs belong to the same class when they imply identical conditional independence statements for conditioning sets of size at most k. They introduce a graphical representation that characterizes these classes, providing the theoretical foundation needed when unrestricted independence information is unavailable.

The resulting k-PC algorithm is a sound constraint-based method for learning this equivalence class. Its target is the collection of graphs consistent with the restricted independence information, rather than a guaranteed unique causal graph. Synthetic and semi-synthetic experiments show more robust discovery than the evaluated baselines with small samples. The contribution connects a practical testing restriction to an explicit account of what causal structure remains identifiable.
neurips-2023-characterization-and-learni.tldr: k-PC learns causal equivalence classes using small conditioning sets, improving robustness in the reported small-sample experiments.

paragraphs: Working memory involves temporarily holding information, combining it, changing it, and retrieving it for ongoing reasoning. WorM is a benchmark designed to evaluate these different capabilities together. It contains ten tasks and one million trials, spanning four functionalities, three domains, and eleven behavioral and neural characteristics of working memory.

The researchers jointly train and test recurrent neural networks and transformers across the tasks. They also include human behavioral results as an upper comparison benchmark. This shared evaluation makes it possible to examine more than whether a model succeeds on one task: it supports comparisons of the patterns that emerge across different memory demands.

The results suggest that the tested AI models reproduce some characteristics associated with human working memory. These include advantages for information presented early or late, known as primacy and recency effects, and clusters or neural correlates specialized for different domains and functions. The experiments also expose limitations in matching human behavior. WorM therefore provides a common resource for studying both successful similarities and remaining gaps across AI, psychology, and neuroscience.
neurips-2023-decoding-the-enigma-benchma.tldr: WorM benchmarks multiple working-memory abilities and finds that tested AI models reproduce some, but not all, human behavioral characteristics.

paragraphs: Diffusion-based purification attempts to remove adversarial perturbations before an image is classified. Evaluating these defenses is difficult because purification creates a very deep, random computational process. An attack can struggle with gradients and memory requirements, so resistance to an existing attack may partly reflect difficulties in attacking the defense.

DiffAttack addresses these obstacles for both DDPM and score-based purification. It introduces an intermediate reconstruction loss designed to disrupt density-gradient estimation and address vanishing or exploding gradients. A segment-wise forward-and-backward procedure also makes gradient computation more memory efficient, allowing the attack to work through the purification process more effectively.

Compared with existing state-of-the-art attacks, DiffAttack reports robust-accuracy decreases exceeding 20% on CIFAR-10 and 10% on ImageNet under the stated infinity-norm budgets of 8/255 and 4/255. Ablations find that applying the added loss at uniformly sampled diffusion steps is more effective than using only initial or final steps. They also find greater robustness with moderate diffusion lengths. These results show why attack quality matters when interpreting the apparent robustness of diffusion defenses.
neurips-2023-diffattack-evasion-attacks-.tldr: DiffAttack improves attacks on diffusion purification by addressing gradient and memory obstacles, substantially reducing reported robust accuracy.

paragraphs: In cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, a team learns to act together while assigning credit to individual agents. Value decomposition separates the team’s value into agent-level components. Most existing approaches rely on Individual Global Max, or related conditions, which constrain how individual action preferences connect to the team’s preferred joint action.

This paper proposes a framework that removes that premise. Each agent has an ego policy responsible for selecting actions and an alter ego value function responsible for credit assignment. An explicit search procedure allows the value factorization to operate without the IGM assumption. Separating these responsibilities creates a different route to coordinating action selection and evaluating contributions.

The framework also introduces anti-ego exploration, intended to keep learning from becoming trapped in a local optimum. The authors describe their method as the first fully IGM-free value decomposition approach and report desirable performance across several cooperative tasks. The stated finding supports the feasibility of value decomposition without its usual structural restriction; the exploration mechanism is a proposed aid against local traps, rather than a stated guarantee of finding a global optimum.
neurips-2023-dual-self-awareness-value-d.tldr: The framework separates action selection from credit assignment and uses explicit search to enable cooperative value decomposition without IGM.

paragraphs: Inferring a gene regulatory network requires understanding how genes and their products influence expression. Two difficulties arise together: regulatory relationships can contain feedback cycles, and noisy observations leave many graph structures plausible. DynGFN aims to represent both cyclic regulation and uncertainty about which dependencies the data support.

The approach relies on access to gene-expression velocity information, estimated through RNA velocity techniques. This changes the problem into identifying a sparse dynamical system: a relatively small set of dependencies describing how expression changes. Feedback loops can then be represented through dynamics over time instead of forcing the regulatory network into an acyclic graph.

Generative Flow Networks are used to estimate a Bayesian posterior over the combinatorial space of possible sparse dependencies. The output therefore represents uncertainty across candidate structures rather than only selecting one graph. The reported results indicate that DynGFN’s posteriors better capture distributions of cyclic structures than the compared state-of-the-art Bayesian structure-learning methods. Its contribution is a way to combine uncertain structure inference with feedback-aware modeling when velocity information is available.
neurips-2023-dyngfn-towards-bayesian-inf.tldr: DynGFN uses expression velocities and GFlowNets to infer uncertain gene regulatory structures that can include feedback cycles.

paragraphs: The paper studies how to recover the geometry of a data space from noisy similarities between points. Its target is a Riemannian metric, which specifies local geometry and supports calculations such as derivatives and geodesic curves. Learning this quantity offers a richer description of the underlying space than estimating isolated pairwise similarities.

The authors assume observed similarities are noisy responses generated by a function of intrinsic geodesic distance. They use a Taylor expansion of squared geodesic distances to build a local regression method for estimating the metric tensor and its derivatives. The framework accommodates continuous measurements, binary responses, and comparative observations, allowing different kinds of similarity evidence to inform the same geometric object.

The theoretical analysis derives convergence rates for the asymptotic bias and variance of the metric estimator. These results characterize how estimation error behaves as data grows. Simulations and applications involving New York City taxi travel times and MNIST digits illustrate the method’s versatility. The contribution links noisy observations to an estimated local geometry from which broader geometric features can be computed.
neurips-2023-estimating-riemannian-metri.tldr: A local regression method estimates manifold geometry and its derivatives from noisy observations related to intrinsic distances.

paragraphs: Regression adjustment uses auxiliary information about experimental subjects to reduce variation in estimated outcomes or treatment effects. This paper examines that idea for a finite population, with particular attention to experiments that expose only a subset of people to treatment. Limiting participation can matter for both practical and ethical reasons.

The authors study estimation of the sample mean, individual treatment effects, and the average treatment effect. Their methods draw on randomized numerical linear algebra to choose a subset of the population on which to run the experiment. This brings the selection of experimental subjects into the same methodological picture as the subsequent regression-adjusted estimation.

The analysis supplies non-asymptotic accuracy bounds, meaning guarantees stated for finite settings rather than only through limiting behavior as sample sizes grow. The authors also demonstrate favorable comparisons with prior approaches. The central contribution is therefore a combination of subset selection, regression adjustment, and finite-data accuracy analysis. It addresses the practical situation where experimenting on an entire population is undesirable while accurate estimation remains important.
neurips-2023-finite-population-regressio.tldr: The paper combines population subsampling and regression adjustment with finite-data accuracy guarantees for mean and treatment-effect estimation.

paragraphs: Membership inference asks whether a particular data point was used to train a model. This paper introduces f-Membership Inference Privacy, a privacy notion that explicitly accounts for realistic attackers’ capabilities under that threat model. The aim is to provide interpretable guarantees while allowing improved utility, such as better classification accuracy.

By analyzing likelihood-ratio membership attacks on stochastic gradient descent, the authors derive a Gaussian family of guarantees called μ-GMIP. Their analysis indicates that ordinary SGD already provides an elementary level of membership privacy, and that adding noise to gradient updates can strengthen it. This is protection within the stated membership-inference framework, with the attacker’s modeled capabilities central to its meaning.

The same analysis yields an analytical attack that requires no shadow models, unlike approaches that train hundreds of them. It also provides a straightforward way to audit the proposed privacy notion. The paper quantifies how factors including batch size, model parameter count, and data characteristics affect membership inference, and demonstrates its method on vision and tabular data. These results connect privacy guarantees to concrete training choices and an accompanying evaluation procedure.
neurips-2023-gaussian-membership-inferen.tldr: The paper develops membership-inference privacy guarantees for SGD and an analytical auditing attack that needs no shadow models.

paragraphs: H-InDex uses knowledge about human hands to develop visual representations for robotic dexterity. The idea is to give reinforcement learning a representation shaped by hand structure before it learns manipulation behavior. This makes human hand pose estimation a source of visual knowledge for difficult robotic control tasks.

The framework has three stages. It first pretrains representations through 3D human hand pose estimation, then adapts them offline using self-supervised keypoint detection. Finally, it performs reinforcement learning with exponential moving average BatchNorm. Across the last two stages, only 0.36% of the pretrained representation’s parameters are modified. This limited adaptation is intended to preserve the knowledge acquired during pretraining while supporting the downstream tasks.

The authors evaluate H-InDex on twelve challenging dexterous manipulation tasks and report that it substantially outperforms strong baselines and recent visual foundation models for motor control. The findings support the usefulness of hand-informed representations in those evaluations. The approach’s distinctive contribution is the combination of targeted pretraining and very limited later modification, connecting perception learned from human hands to visual reinforcement learning for manipulation.
neurips-2023-h-index-visual-reinforcemen.tldr: H-InDex transfers hand-pose-informed visual representations to dexterous reinforcement learning while modifying only a small fraction of representation parameters.

paragraphs: Large gradient-descent steps can make training loss oscillate instead of decreasing at every iteration. This paper studies that edge-of-stability behavior for logistic regression on linearly separable data. It asks both whether learning still converges over longer timescales and which solution direction the optimization process implicitly favors.

The authors prove that logistic loss can be minimized over a long timescale with any constant stepsize, despite local oscillations. They also decompose the parameter trajectory into two parts. Its component along the hard-margin support-vector-machine direction grows without bound, while its component perpendicular to that direction converges to a fixed vector minimizing a strongly convex potential.

These findings explain how increasing parameter magnitude and a stable directional preference can coexist with irregular short-term loss behavior. The paper also shows that exponential loss may instead lead to catastrophic divergence in this regime. Numerical simulations agree with the theoretical results. The conclusions extend small-stepsize analyses for logistic regression, with linear separability and the choice of loss remaining essential parts of the stated setting.
neurips-2023-implicit-bias-of-gradient-d.tldr: For linearly separable logistic regression, any constant gradient-descent stepsize retains long-term loss minimization and a max-margin directional bias.

paragraphs: Comparing the internal representations of many neural networks can be computationally expensive, especially when comparisons require probing models with data. This paper proposes reducing representational similarity to distances between elements of convolutional filter subspaces. The goal is to make large collections of models easier to compare.

The simplification depends on a particular representation: convolutional filters are written as linear combinations of filter atoms, with the combination coefficients shared across networks. Under that setup, similarity can be assessed through cosine distances between the respective atoms. The authors report computation reductions of millions of times relative to popular probing-based methods.

Theoretical and empirical evidence shows that this cheaper measure remains strongly linearly correlated with established probing-based similarity metrics and is robust to probing data. Applications include federated learning, continual learning, and analysis of training dynamics, all settings involving numerous models. The result is a highly efficient comparison method under the shared-coefficient construction; strong correlation supports its usefulness without implying that it produces exactly the same values as every existing representation metric.
neurips-2023-inner-product-based-neural-.tldr: With shared filter-decomposition coefficients, cosine distances between filter atoms provide an efficient proxy for neural-network representational similarity.

paragraphs: A non-negative tensor is a multidimensional array whose entries are non-negative. Traditional tensor decomposition often seeks a low-rank representation, creating challenges in choosing the target rank and finding a global optimum. This paper introduces many-body approximation, which controls the relationships among tensor dimensions through a different modeling approach.

The method interprets a tensor as a probability distribution and each tensor mode as a random variable. An energy-based model represents interactions among those variables. The authors show that the model can be globally optimized by minimizing KL divergence, a measure of discrepancy between distributions. They argue that specifying interactions provides a more intuitive control than choosing tensor ranks.

The paper also visualizes interactions between modes as tensor networks and establishes a nontrivial relationship between many-body and low-rank approximation. This connects the new formulation to familiar tensor representations while retaining its interaction-based perspective. Experiments demonstrate effectiveness in tensor approximation and completion. The contribution is a globally optimizable formulation in which modeling choices concern which dimensions interact, offering another way to organize and recover multidimensional non-negative data.
neurips-2023-many-body-approximation-for.tldr: Many-body approximation models tensor dimensions as interacting random variables, enabling global KL-divergence optimization without selecting a low rank.

paragraphs: Michelangelo generates 3D shapes from images or text by first aligning how those different kinds of information are represented. The motivation is that directly learning an image-to-shape or text-to-shape mapping can produce shapes that do not match the condition. The paper attributes this difficulty to the distributional gap between 3D shapes and the other modalities.

The framework has two components. A Shape-Image-Text-Aligned Variational Auto-Encoder places shapes in a latent space aligned with images and text. Its transformer decoder reconstructs detailed 3D neural fields from those shape embeddings. A conditional Aligned Shape Latent Diffusion Model then learns a probabilistic mapping from image or text representations into the aligned shape space.

This division makes alignment a foundation for generation: the generative model works with shape representations already connected to the conditioning modalities. The reported experiments produce higher-quality, more diverse shapes that better match the meaning of visual or textual inputs. These findings support the usefulness of the shared representation for cross-modal 3D generation, with the benefits demonstrated through the authors’ experimental comparisons.
neurips-2023-michelangelo-conditional-3d.tldr: Michelangelo aligns shape, image, and text representations before diffusion-based generation to improve the quality and condition matching of 3D shapes.

paragraphs: Masked auto-encoders learn by reconstructing hidden parts of an input from the parts that remain visible. This paper develops that idea into a self-supervised framework intended to work across diverse modalities. Its motivation is that much self-supervised learning progress has concentrated on a few domains and often depends on domain-specific knowledge.

MetaMAE interprets each reconstruction problem as a meta-learning task. The visible tokens provide information that adapts a Transformer-based learner to predict the missing tokens. Building on this interpretation, the method uses gradient-based meta-learning to adapt the encoder’s amortized latent representation and improve reconstruction. Task contrastive learning then aligns the original and adapted latent representations.

That alignment is intended to teach the encoder to represent task-specific information more effectively, connecting its initial representation to one refined through adaptation. The authors evaluate MetaMAE on DABS, a modality-agnostic self-supervised learning benchmark, and report significant improvements over prior baselines. The contribution is both a reinterpretation of masked reconstruction and a concrete method derived from it, with the benchmark results supporting its use across the evaluated modalities.
neurips-2023-modality-agnostic-self-supe.tldr: MetaMAE treats masked reconstruction as meta-learning and aligns adapted representations to improve self-supervised learning across modalities.

paragraphs: Multi-source unsupervised domain adaptation uses several source domains to help a model work on a target domain without target labels. Updating an entire shared network to reconcile those domains can be expensive and difficult. Multi-Prompt Alignment instead builds on prompt learning as a computationally economical way to adapt a high-capacity model.

For each source–target pair, the method learns an individual prompt using a contrastive loss to reduce the domain gap. It then passes the learned prompts through an auto-encoding process to denoise them. Maximizing agreement among the reconstructed prompts aligns what the different source domains contribute, connecting pair-specific adaptation with a shared result.

The authors also show that the subspace learned by auto-encoding can generalize to a streamlined set of target domains, improving practical efficiency. Experiments report state-of-the-art results on three datasets, including average accuracy of 54.1% on DomainNet. These findings support prompt alignment as an effective approach in the evaluated multi-source setting, where adapting and reconciling prompts replaces the expensive emphasis on updating a full shared feature network.
neurips-2023-multi-prompt-alignment-for-.tldr: Multi-Prompt Alignment learns, denoises, and reconciles domain-specific prompts for efficient multi-source unsupervised adaptation.

paragraphs: Camera trajectories estimated from monocular video are useful for understanding environments and activities, but reconstruction pipelines can fail on complex footage. Measuring those failures is difficult when videos lack known 3D geometry or camera poses. Obtaining that ground truth after recording may be prohibitively expensive or impossible.

Object Reprojection Error offers an evaluation protocol based on lightweight annotations that track static objects through video. It measures reprojection error for those objects to benchmark estimated camera trajectories. Because these object tracklets can be annotated in existing as well as new footage, the protocol broadens the range of videos on which trajectory estimation can be assessed.

The authors find high rank correlation between ORE and standard metrics that require ground truth. This supports using ORE to compare the ordering of trajectory-estimation results when richer annotations are unavailable. They also use videos and annotations from Ego4D-EgoTracks to create EgoStatic, a large and diverse dataset for evaluating camera trajectories in natural settings. The contribution combines a more accessible evaluation signal with a dataset built around that signal.
neurips-2023-object-reprojection-error-o.tldr: ORE evaluates camera trajectories using lightweight static-object tracks and correlates strongly with rankings from ground-truth-based metrics.

paragraphs: Radiology reports communicate imaging findings between radiologists and other clinicians. RaLEs treats these reports as a distinct language domain and introduces a benchmark covering multiple forms of understanding and generation. Its seven evaluations include extracting anatomical and disease entities and their relationships, selecting procedures, and summarizing reports.

The researchers compare models developed for general language, biomedicine, clinical text, and radiology across the benchmark. Evaluating this range on shared tasks helps determine whether progress in a broader language domain carries over to the specific demands of radiology reports. It also moves evaluation beyond methods designed for a single report-processing task.

The results show that advances in general and biomedical language modeling do not necessarily translate into improvements in radiology. Improved general-domain models can perform comparably to smaller models specialized for clinical language. Existing pretrained models also show limited performance on RaLEs, motivating further development of domain-specific self-supervised models. The benchmark provides a common way to measure that progress across several relevant tasks, rather than assuming that success elsewhere establishes radiology capability.
neurips-2023-rales-a-benchmark-for-radio.tldr: RaLEs evaluates seven radiology language tasks and shows that progress in broader language domains does not necessarily transfer.

paragraphs: Face-recognition systems can perform unevenly across demographic groups. Many mitigation efforts focus on training data, training penalties, or changes to predictions. This paper identifies neural network architecture itself as a source of bias, making the model’s structural design an additional target for improving fairness.

The authors conduct a neural architecture search explicitly aimed at fairness, combined with a search over hyperparameters. This evaluates model design and training choices together, seeking architectures that improve the relationship between recognition accuracy and fairness. The approach shifts part of the mitigation effort toward selecting a better model structure before relying on interventions around a fixed architecture.

On CelebA and VGGFace2, the resulting suite of models is reported to Pareto-dominate the compared high-performance architectures and existing mitigation methods in accuracy and fairness, often by large margins. Pareto dominance indicates improvement without sacrificing the other criterion. The authors also report generalization to other datasets and sensitive attributes. These findings establish architecture search as a promising fairness intervention in the evaluated settings, expanding the set of model-development decisions relevant to demographic performance.
neurips-2023-rethinking-bias-mitigation-.tldr: Joint architecture and hyperparameter search produces face-recognition models with better accuracy–fairness tradeoffs in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Probability models need both expressive shapes and a way to ensure their total probability is one. Squared Neural Families, or SNEFYs, construct distributions by taking the squared Euclidean norm of a neural network’s output and normalizing it relative to a base measure. Squaring provides the non-negative quantity needed to form a density.

The difficult part of this construction is computing the normalizing constant. Using reasoning related to connections between infinitely wide neural networks and Gaussian processes, the authors obtain closed-form constants in many cases of interest. This allows flexible neural-network-based densities whose normalization can still be handled exactly in those cases.

The paper also establishes useful structural properties: SNEFYs strictly generalize classical exponential families, remain within the family under conditioning, and have tractable marginal distributions. These properties support working with partially observed variables and distributions conditioned on available information. Applications illustrate density estimation, conditional density estimation, and estimation with missing data. The main contribution is a probability-model family that combines neural flexibility with tractable operations needed for these statistical tasks.
neurips-2023-squared-neural-families-a-n.tldr: SNEFYs turn squared neural-network outputs into flexible probability models with closed-form normalization in many cases and tractable conditioning and marginals.

paragraphs: State-space models offer simple and efficient structures for processing sequences. However, a lack of nonlinear activation along the time direction restricts their capacity. This paper investigates whether introducing nonlinearities between stacked layers can supply the expressive power needed to model complicated relationships between input and output sequences.

The authors prove that stacking state-space models with layer-wise nonlinear activation is sufficient to approximate any continuous sequence-to-sequence relationship. The result identifies an architectural route to universal approximation: complex sequence mappings can be represented through the combination of stacked state-space layers and nonlinear transformations between them. It is a statement about representational capacity.

The paper also finds, both theoretically and empirically, that these models do not fundamentally eliminate exponentially decaying memory. Thus, stronger approximation capacity coexists with a continuing tendency for information from the past to fade exponentially. Numerical verifications support the theoretical findings. Taken together, the results distinguish two properties that can otherwise be conflated: the ability to express complex sequence relationships and the behavior of memory over time.
neurips-2023-state-space-models-with-lay.tldr: Layer-wise nonlinearities make stacked state-space models universal approximators, while exponentially decaying memory remains.

paragraphs: This paper analyzes how convolutional network design influences what models can represent and how much data they need. The authors prove that depth growing logarithmically with input dimension is sufficient for universal approximation. They also show that CNNs can learn sparse functions with sample requirements growing roughly as squared logarithms of input dimension, supporting efficient capture of long-range sparse correlations.

The construction combines multiple channels and downsampling as depth increases. To separate the effects of weight sharing and locality, the authors compare convolutional, locally connected, and fully connected networks on a simple regression task. Locally connected networks preserve locality while removing the shared weights used by CNNs.

On that task, locally connected networks require at least linearly many samples in input dimension, while CNNs need only roughly squared-logarithmic sample counts. Fully connected networks require at least quadratically many samples, whereas locally connected networks can learn with roughly linear counts. These task-specific separations quantify distinct benefits from weight sharing and locality. The proofs connect those benefits to the different symmetries each architectural constraint breaks during learning.
neurips-2023-theoretical-analysis-of-the.tldr: The paper proves CNN approximation and sample-efficiency results and separates the learning benefits of locality and weight sharing.

paragraphs: Standard analyses of stochastic gradient descent often assume its learning-rate scale is tuned using properties of the objective, such as a smoothness constant that may be unknown. This paper studies what happens when the stepsize decreases as η divided by the square root of the iteration number, but η is any positive value.

For smooth objectives, the authors prove that this untuned SGD scheme still achieves an order-optimal gradient-norm convergence rate of approximately T to the minus one-quarter, up to logarithmic factors. However, the bound has an exponential dependence on the smoothness constant. They show that this dependence is unavoidable for the scheme, even when gradients contain no stochastic noise.

The paper then analyzes Normalized SGD, AMSGrad, and AdaGrad. These adaptive method families avoid that exponential dependence without requiring knowledge of the smoothness parameter or bounded stochastic gradients. The results explain why an attractive iteration-rate exponent alone can hide severe optimization costs. They also provide theoretical support for using adaptive methods to handle large gradients when the information needed to tune ordinary SGD is unavailable.
neurips-2023-two-sides-of-one-coin-the-l.tldr: Untuned SGD retains an optimal rate exponent but suffers unavoidable exponential smoothness dependence that the analyzed adaptive methods avoid.

paragraphs: Origin attribution asks whether a particular image was generated by a specified model. Existing approaches can require special changes during training or generation, making them unsuitable for pretrained models that did not include those procedures. This paper develops an attribution method that does not require such alterations and is designed to work across model types.

The method reverse-engineers the generation process by trying to recover an input that makes the candidate model reconstruct the image. The authors analyze how difficult this inversion is for images generated by that model compared with other images. They then use the reconstruction loss as evidence for deciding whether the candidate model is the image’s source.

The reported results show that this approach effectively distinguishes a model’s generated images from both real images and images generated by other models. Its practical significance is that attribution can be based on the existing generator’s reconstruction behavior, without adding a special attribution procedure to its training or generation pipeline. The task remains attribution to a specified candidate model, with reconstruction error providing the decision signal.
neurips-2023-where-did-i-come-from-origi.tldr: The method attributes images to a candidate generator using inversion reconstruction loss, without modifying training or generation.
